### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5430b4a40cf298d0784ea3a9f8aabdf36068d761` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4eebbc4b479118203ab05a0ad5fd88336559abe4` — the merge of head `35660b555d394212e25efb94f270a27825a5d8e2` into base `5430b4a40cf298d0784ea3a9f8aabdf36068d761`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4eebbc4b479118203ab05a0ad5fd88336559abe4 && git checkout 4eebbc4b479118203ab05a0ad5fd88336559abe4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5430b4a40cf298d0784ea3a9f8aabdf36068d761 35660b555d394212e25efb94f270a27825a5d8e2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5430b4a40cf298d0784ea3a9f8aabdf36068d761 && git merge --no-ff 35660b555d394212e25efb94f270a27825a5d8e2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5430b4a40cf298d0784ea3a9f8aabdf36068d761
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0d2b827809368c9c070bd465bc1307dbd7bc1e6e`
Local-runs: probe — the seat asked for the consumer-package suites of these schemas (dispatch-gates misses them); run on a `git archive` export of the head tree, repo checkout untouched, after a filtered `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm turbo run build --concurrency=2 --filter='@objectstack/cli...'` (64/64 tasks). Runs:
- spec · `vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/stack src/compose src/migrations src/api/error-code-ledger`: 57 files, 1679 tests passed.
- runtime · `src/artifact-collections.public-reader.test.ts`, `src/artifact-collections.test.ts`: 2 files, 25 passed.
- metadata · `src/owner-stamp-residual-build-boot.test.ts`, `src/plugin-artifact-packages-attribution.test.ts`, `src/plugin-artifact-forward-conversion-retired-after.test.ts`: 3 files, 43 passed.
- metadata-protocol · `src/protocol.install-manifest-id.test.ts`: 19 passed. core · `src/capability-composition.test.ts`: 13 passed.
- cli · `src/utils/artifact-packages.test.ts`, `test/migrate-meta-composed.test.ts`, `test/serve-config-boot-residual.integration.test.ts`: 3 files, 26 passed. The two e2e files (`test/build-multi-package-artifact.e2e.test.ts`, `test/compile-artifact-packages.e2e.test.ts`) are outside the default projects and did not run.
- Throwaway probe, 27 verdicts, run against head source and against the merge-base `stack.zod.ts` (`12b14462`); the judgments in ① cite it.
- New pins run against merge-base source: additive, hand-built and runtime round-trip pins red, control green, the one/two-residual pin red on its wording assertion only (N3).
Scope: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.define-stack-packages-residual-second-app-refused.ts` (hits); `packages/spec/src/stack.test.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.public-reader.test.ts`; the changeset and PR body (prose, sentence by sentence) + read at head: `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `artifactItemSlot`, `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE`), `packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/collection-item-owner-stamp.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`, `.changeset/32586-…`, `.changeset/32810-…`, `docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`, HotCRM `0009f58` (`objectstack.config.ts`, `test/helpers/composed-stack.ts`)

Check-runs at review time (2026-11-13T08:39Z): 47 success, 11 skipped, 6 in progress (Test Core 7/8 and 8/8, Test UI 1/16 and 16/16, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace), no failure; `Check Changeset` success. Tests and type check are not yet a full gate verdict. `main` moved `12b14462` → `4079b06b` with no change to any path of this diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- Narrowing arm, reproduced and fixed: a preserve suite plus one top-level app no body declares, the manifest-id body holding one app, is accepted at merge-base and refused at head with `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION` 422, under a `module` and an `app` manifest. **Right.**
- Widening arm, reproduced and fixed: an additive artifact whose top level repeats two bodies' apps is refused 422 at merge-base and accepted at head; the reader round trip likewise. **Right.**
- Whole delta (T top-level apps, R of them residual, B apps in the manifest-id body): the old rule refuses T ≥ 2, the new one refuses R ≥ 1 and B + R ≥ 2. Newly refused ⇔ T = R = 1 and B ≥ 1, exactly the declared shape. Nothing else previously accepted is refused. **Right.**
- Newly accepted beyond the named example: copies of other bodies' apps beside one residual app, where the manifest-id body has none or no body has that id. The load path puts one app under the manifest id there. **Right**, inside "judged by the residual rule".
- The two doors agree: a `composeStacks` result that carries `packages[]` and passes is accepted by strict `defineStack` (a flat composition of a nested artifact was refused at merge-base); hand-built equivalents of two compositions `composeStacks` refuses are refused by `defineStack` with the same package and count. **Right.**
- One judge: `residualSingleAppFinding` holds the predicate (`isResidualTopLevelItem`), the owner id, the in-body apps, the threshold and the sentence; a door supplies the subject, the residual labels and the remedy. The `composeStacks` finding is the same template string for string. **Right.** No second copy.
- Mirror of the load path: `unclaimedTopLevel` walks `apps`, claims by name and owns under `manifest.id ?? id`; the judge reads the same three. `packages/metadata` is untouched. **Right.**
- Unchanged: a stack without `packages[]` (finding byte-identical at merge-base and head), `strict: false`, manifest types other than `app`/`module`, a stack with no manifest, `packages: []` (same verdict, wording moves, N2). **Right.**
- No export moves, no new error code, no schema shape change; `registry.ts` is git-ignored, so no generated artefact is owed in the diff.
- Exposure: no non-test code in `packages/**`, `examples/**`, `apps/**` or HotCRM hands a `packages[]` stack to strict `defineStack`. metadata, metadata-protocol, core and cli have no non-test `defineStack(`/`composeStacks(` call; their tests call the producers on per-package inputs, `strict: false` inputs or config literals, none passing a `packages[]` value to strict `defineStack`. None names `validateSingleApp`.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is correct: `yes` for the widened accept set, and the one permitted arm is `(narrowing)` because that arm is the breaking one; `narrowed` outranks `added`. `@objectstack/spec` minor matches the kind and the sibling entries (#32586, #32810). No runtime changeset is owed (test-only). The semantic entry has the five `SemanticMigration` fields, the `adr-0087: registered` id equals the entry id, and the BREAKING banner carries Before / Now / Unchanged / Fix. `Skills-docs: none` holds: no skill, docs page or example hands a `packages[]` stack to `defineStack`.

Prose faces against the code at head:
- Changeset Before, Now, Unchanged, Fix: each bullet holds, with N1, N2 and N4.
- Entry `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`: hold. `surface`: N1.
- Docblocks of `validateSingleApp`, `StackSingleAppViolationError`, `collectComposedSingleAppErrors`, `residualSingleAppFinding`: hold, with N5.
- The five new `describe`/`it` strings: hold (N3). The PR body's example finding matches the emitted text.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Claim 6846776794 said `yes` / `semantic`; the PR and changeset say `yes (narrowing)` / `narrowed`; amendment 6846967975 records the correction. Both directions are measured above.
- File surface: five files, all inside the claim plus amendment 6846967975 (the runtime test).
- #33069: not touched, not fixed, not worsened. `validateNamespacePrefix` runs before `validateSingleApp` and is outside the diff; a multi-namespace additive artifact gets the same `STACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_INVALID` at merge-base and head. When #33069 lands, such an artifact reaches this judge, which already reads it per body.
- ADR-0019's enforcement log ends at #32586 and still lists a hand-built `packages[]` body as not judged; governed text, correctly not edited here.
- PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

Holds. Strict `defineStack` now reads a `packages[]` stack as the load path registers it, through the judge #32898 already gave `composeStacks`, and leaves the authored (no `packages[]`) route on its old line. The order's five steps are met: shared implementation, docblock corrected, four pins plus the round trip on the reader's side, changeset at the named path. Judging on the stack manifest's `type` is the reading `composeStacks` uses, so the doors cannot split on it.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits:
- N1 · the declaration line's "(or two such apps) … where it was accepted" and the entry `surface`'s "or two or more such apps" name no newly refused shape: two undeclared top-level apps were already refused at merge-base with the same code and status. Over-inclusive, safe direction.
- N2 · a `packages[]` stack that was already refused (two undeclared top-level apps, or `packages: []` with two apps) now gets the residual sentence in place of "package 'X' defines N …", and an `app` manifest loses the "fold them into one app" remedy on that path. Code, status and header unchanged; the changeset does not mention the rewording.
- N3 · pin 3's "refuses two" half does not discriminate by verdict (merge-base refuses it too; only the wording assertion turns red). No pin covers the copy-plus-one-residual widening, or a manifest-id body of an unjudged type.
- N4 · the changeset's Widened line names `resolveArtifactCollections` output as accepted without the #33069 limit (differently-namespaced packages are still refused earlier). The PR body states the limit.
- N5 · `residualSingleAppFinding`'s docblock says `door` "only names" the residual apps, but `door.residual` also enumerates them, so the count comes from the door. The two doors agree today; a third could differ.

- 先看：`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` 里的 `residualSingleAppFinding` 与 `validateSingleApp` 调用处。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/stack.test.ts`，预期全绿。
- 需要你做的：18.4.0 冻结期间不入队；是等解冻还是向 triage 申请例外，请在线程决策卡上选。
